title: Cap-and-Spill: Two-Pass CUDA-Graph MoE Dispatch Without Worst-Case Padding

contributions.purpose: Reduce padding waste in CUDA-graph-captured MoE AllToAll dispatch while keeping fixed buffer sizes.
contributions.mechanism: Propose Cap-and-Spill, a two-pass CUDA-graph-compatible dispatch algorithm using quantile-based buffer capacity (C = Q99) for the first pass and a second pass for overflow tokens.
contributions.evaluation: Both passes use fixed buffers, maintaining CUDA-graph compatibility; unconditional two-pass execution outperforms conditional execution by eliminating synchronization overhead.
contributions.source_quote: We propose Cap-and-Spill, a two-pass CUDA-graph-compatible MoE dispatch algorithm that uses quantile-based buffer capacity to reduce padding waste while handling overflow tokens in a second pass.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate the latency benefit of the method with correctness guarantees.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmark Cap-and-Spill on 8xA100 NVLink with Mixtral-8x7B routing traces against worst-case-padded and oracle eager dispatch.
contributions.evaluation: 33.9% mean latency reduction (1077 us -> 712 us), recovering 53.2% of the gap to oracle eager dispatch, with bitwise-equal exact correctness.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate 33.9% mean latency reduction (1077 us -> 712 us) on 8xA100 NVLink with Mixtral-8x7B routing traces, recovering 53.2% of the gap to oracle eager dispatch while maintaining exact correctness.

contributions.purpose: Characterize MoE routing distributions to justify the quantile operating point.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze the heavy-tailed nature of per-peer token counts (Cmax/mu = 8.4x) and evaluate percentile choices.
contributions.evaluation: Show the 99th percentile is the optimal operating point, balancing buffer reduction (2.69x) with minimal overflow (5.4%).
contributions.source_quote: We characterize the heavy-tailed nature of MoE routing distributions (Cmax/mu = 8.4x) and show that the 99th percentile provides the optimal operating point, balancing buffer reduction (2.69x) with minimal overflow (5.4%).

self_declared_provenance.quote: While these systems optimize various aspects of MoE execution, none specifically address the buffer padding waste inherent in CUDA-graph-captured AllToAll operations.

Current approaches either forgo CUDA graphs entirely (sacrificing throughput) or use worst-case buffer allocation (wasting memory and bandwidth). Our work bridges this gap by introducing a two-pass dispatch strategy that maintains CUDA-graph compatibility while substantially reducing buffer requirements through quantile-based capacity allocation.
